extra.message: renderReportPdf() builds the shell command 'wkhtmltopdf '+source+' '+layout+' '+output and executes it with new ProcessBuilder("sh","-c",command). Both source and layout are free-text fields taken directly from the ImportExportView UI (reportSource.getValue(), reportLayout.getValue()) with no validation or escaping, so shell metacharacters in either field are interpreted by /bin/sh, allowing arbitrary OS command execution.

directoryQueue() concatenates the client-controlled 'queueTitle' cookie directly into a SQL string passed to jdbc.queryForList("SELECT name, email, title FROM contact WHERE title = '" + title + "'"). An attacker can set an arbitrary queueTitle cookie value containing SQL (e.g. a UNION SELECT) to exfiltrate arbitrary table data.

scoreContacts() takes a 'rule' string directly from the request body and evaluates it with SpelExpressionParser against a StandardEvaluationContext (parser.parseExpression(rule).getValue(ctx)) with no sandboxing or expression allowlist. SpEL allows arbitrary type/method invocation (e.g. T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec(...)), so a caller with any valid 'organizations:read' API key can achieve remote code execution.

restoreContactBatch() Base64-decodes the client-supplied 'batch' request parameter and feeds it straight into `new ObjectInputStream(new ByteArrayInputStream(bytes))` then calls readObject() with no class filtering. A crafted serialized Java gadget chain submitted here results in remote code execution on deserialization.

byAccount() builds the LDAP filter '(&(objectClass=person)(sAMAccountName='+account+'))' by directly concatenating the 'account' value, which comes unsanitized from the @PathVariable in ApiController.staff() (/api/v1/directory/staff/{account}). An attacker can inject LDAP filter syntax to alter query logic or perform blind LDAP injection.

findFeedContact() builds an XPath expression "//contact[contains(@name,'"+name+"')]" by directly concatenating the user-supplied 'name' parameter (from the 'Search partner feed' UI) and evaluates it against the partner feed DOM, allowing XPath injection to alter the query or read unintended nodes/attributes.

importContactsXml() creates XMLInputFactory.newInstance() and an XMLStreamReader over attacker-controlled bytes (the uploaded partner XML feed) without disabling IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES or SUPPORT_DTD. A crafted feed with a DOCTYPE declaring an external or parameter entity can read local files or trigger SSRF during parsing.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: findFeedContact() parses the staged partner-feed.xml with DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance().newDocumentBuilder() without disabling DOCTYPE declarations or external entity resolution (no setFeature calls to disallow-doctype-decl / external-general-entities). Since that file's content originates from an attacker-controlled upload (importContactsXml), a planted XXE payload is processed again on every search.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: checkReachability() opens an HTTP connection to any URL starting with 'http' with no host allowlist (unlike createWebhook's validateUrl(), which restricts to '.example.test'/'localhost'). Reachable from the 'Check reachability' button in the webhook dialog, this lets an authenticated staff user make the server fetch arbitrary internal/cloud-metadata URLs (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/...) and view the response status/message.

importFromUrl() fetches 'sourceUrl' via http.get().uri(sourceUrl).retrieve().body(byte[].class) with validation limited to a 'startsWith("http")' check and a 2000-char length cap — no host allowlist or block of internal/link-local addresses. A staff user can make the server request internal-only or cloud-metadata endpoints through the 'Import document from URL' dialog, and the response bytes are stored and exposed as a document.

previewImport() resolves the client-supplied 'X-Import-Ref' header directly against Path.of(storagePath).resolve("imports") with no sanitization of '..' sequences, then reads and returns the file's content. A header such as 'X-Import-Ref: ../../application.yml' lets an API-key holder read arbitrary files on the server's filesystem.

importContacts() resolves importsDir.resolve(filename) using the raw client-supplied upload file name (ImportExportView passes e.getFileName() straight through, and importContactsArchive passes the raw zip entry name) with no '..'/'/' checks, unlike DocumentService.upload which sanitizes with StringUtils.cleanPath and rejects traversal sequences. A crafted filename or zip entry name (e.g. '../../../etc/cron.d/x') can write outside importsDir.

exportContactSheet() writes to `new File(importsDir.toFile(), targetName)` where targetName is a free-text field from the 'Prepare delivery bridge file' UI, validated only for blankness/length — no traversal check. A name like '../../../../etc/passwd' (if permissions allow) or any path outside importsDir lets staff users overwrite files elsewhere on disk.

reportEscalations() reads the organization id straight from the client-supplied 'X-Org-Id' header and returns that organization's escalation subjects/statuses, with no integrations.authenticate(...) call or any other access check — unlike every other endpoint in this controller, which requires an X-API-Key with a matching scope. Any caller can enumerate another organization's escalation data just by setting the header.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: console() calls JWT.decode(grant), which only base64-decodes the token and does NOT verify its signature, then trusts the 'organization' claim to look up and return that organization's plan/status/documents. Anyone can mint an arbitrary unsigned/self-signed JWT with any 'organization' claim and retrieve that organization's console data.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: launch() mints the NORTHSTAR_PORTAL cookie from the client-supplied 'organization' query parameter and a bare sequential counter, with no signature, HMAC, or authentication of the caller. portal() later trusts this unsigned cookie value to decide which organization's data to return, so any caller can mint a valid-looking portal session for an arbitrary organization UUID.

@CrossOrigin(originPatterns = "*", allowCredentials = "true") on the /partner/portal endpoint allows any origin to issue credentialed (cookie-bearing) cross-site requests, so a malicious page can read a victim's NORTHSTAR_PORTAL-scoped organization data cross-origin.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message:
badge() writes the 'label' @PathVariable directly into the HTML response body ("
" + label + "
") with no HTML-encoding, so a request such as /partner/badge/ reflects executable script into the text/html response.

The @AnonymousAllowed embed/:id view takes the organization id straight from the route parameter (or an unsigned cookie it sets from the 'viewer' query parameter) and loads/renders that organization's name and status with no token verification or authorization check, letting any anonymous visitor enumerate organizations by UUID.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The /api/v1/configuration endpoint returns the raw spring.datasource.password (bound as storeCredential/"datastoreCredential") and the core-mock credential in its JSON response to any caller holding a valid API key scoped only to 'organizations:read', exposing the database password to any integration partner.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: openSealedEnvelope() decrypts partner envelopes with a hardcoded, static AES key ("NorthstarEnvKey1") and IV ("NorthstarEnvIv16") literal in source. Anyone who reads the source/bytecode can decrypt intercepted envelopes or forge new ones, defeating the envelope's confidentiality/integrity guarantee.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: SharedReferenceController encrypts/decrypts the document-reference token with a hardcoded static AES key and IV. Because the key/IV are fixed literals, an attacker who reads the source can forge valid /shared/reference/{ref} tokens for arbitrary document UUIDs, bypassing the intended issuance control and reading any CustomerDocument's metadata regardless of visibility.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: management.endpoints.web.exposure.include lists health,info,env,heapdump,beans, and SecurityConfig.java permits all requests to /actuator/** with no authentication (`auth.requestMatchers(...,"/actuator/**").permitAll()`). This makes /actuator/env (all resolved config including secrets) and /actuator/heapdump (a full JVM heap dump likely containing the datastore password, session-signing key, and live session tokens) readable by anyone, unauthenticated.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: test() posts to "http://alarms.northstar.test/v1/incident?key="+coreCredential, placing the shared core-mock credential directly in the request URL. URLs are routinely captured in proxy/load-balancer/web-server access logs in plaintext, leaking the credential to anyone with log access.

cwe: CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings

extra.message: pushAccountSummary() sends the reporting bridge key and organization billing/health data as a form-urlencoded POST body to http://accounting-bridge.northstar.test (plain HTTP, not HTTPS), so the bridgeKey credential and sensitive account data are transmitted in cleartext and can be captured by a network intermediary.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: http.headers(headers->headers.frameOptions(frame->frame.disable())) disables X-Frame-Options for the entire application, not just the /partner embed paths that need framing, removing clickjacking protection from the login page and all authenticated admin/CRM screens.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

extra.message: http.sessionManagement(session->session.sessionFixation(fixation->fixation.none())) disables Spring Security's default session-fixation protection application-wide, so the session identifier is not rotated on login, enabling session-fixation attacks.

portalDigest() hashes the customer portal access code with unsalted MD5 (DigestUtils.md5DigestAsHex). If the contact table is ever exfiltrated, these unsalted MD5 digests can be cracked quickly via rainbow tables, recovering the original portal codes used to open shared customer documents.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: deskDigest() derives the support desk passphrase verifier using PBKDF2WithHmacSHA1 with only 1024 iterations and a single hardcoded salt ("northstar-desk") shared by every account, instead of a unique per-user random salt and a modern iteration count. This both allows faster offline brute-forcing and means identical passphrases across users hash identically.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: The NORTHSTAR_EMBED cookie, which carries the organization-identifying viewer session value, is created via plain `new Cookie("NORTHSTAR_EMBED", viewer)` with no Secure, HttpOnly, or SameSite attributes set, so it can be read by client-side script and sent over a plaintext connection.

run() hardcodes the literal password "DemoPass123!" and uses it for every seeded account including the PLATFORM_ADMIN account (admin@northstar.local), applied automatically whenever the user table is empty at startup. If this initializer runs in a reachable environment, the admin account is protected only by a credential visible in source.
